newsitem.title: USA: U.S. govt not looking to boost heating oil supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. govt not looking to boost heating oil supply.

text.p: The U.S. Energy Department is watching heating oil stock levels but is not considering any moves to intervene in oil markets to bolster supplies ahead of this winter, deputy assistant energy secretary Kyle Simpson said on Tuesday.

With heating oil stocks lower than they were at this time in 1995 and 1994, consumer advocates Citizen Action on Tuesday said the government should sell oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve and buy heating oil for delivery, including imports, to prevent a spike in heating oil prices this winter.
"We don't have any intention of looking at that at all," Simpson said, explaining that the government had no legal authority to use the emergency crude oil stockpile for that purpose.
Proposals to reauthorize the law governing the Strategic Petroleum Reserve after October do not include any measures that would expand the department's authority that far, he added.
Simpson said it was "a little too early to tell" whether heating oil supplies would be a problem this winter and said the department would "continue to monitor" inventories.
The Energy Information Administration last week reported that U.S. heating oil stocks at the end of August stood at 109 million barrels, down from 130 million barrels a year ago.
